;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mali War]]
**Gunmen on motorbikes attack a [[military base]] in [[Bamba, Gao Region|Bamba]], [[Gao Region|Gao]], [[Mali]], killing at least 25 [[Mali Armed Forces|soldiers]]. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-04/07/c_138952410.htm (Xinhuanet)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/04/20-malian-soldiers-killed-attack-military-base-200406103504731.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**British [[department store]] retailer [[Debenhams]] files for administration due to "unprecedented" circumstances caused by the [[United Kingdom]]'s coronavirus lockdown. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-52182199 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] is admitted to [[intensive care]] at [[St Thomas' Hospital]] in [[London]] as his [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] symptoms worsen. [[Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs|Foreign Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]], as [[First Secretary of State]], will assume Johnson's duties while he remains in the ICU. [https://www.itv.com/news/2020-04-06/prime-minister-boris-johnson-moved-to-intensive-care-after-being-admitted-to-hospital-with-coronavirus/ (ITV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 833 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest number of deaths recorded in a single day, bringing the country's death toll to 8,911 and the number of cases to 98,010. Health Minister [[Olivier Véran]] says, "We have not reached the end of the ascent of this epidemic." [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-52191889 (BBC News)]
****[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] eases some lockdown restrictions for people on the [[autism spectrum]] following the requests of disability groups. [https://metro.co.uk/2020/04/02/france-eases-lockdown-autistic-people-can-go-reassuring-places-12499265 (''Metro'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Barbados]]
****[[Barbados]] reports its first death from COVID-19, an 81-year-old man with [[diabetes]] who recently travelled to the United Kingdom. [https://www.voice-online.co.uk/news/world-news/2020/04/06/barbados-records-first-covid-19-death/ (Voice Online)]

;Law and crime
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Ivory Coast]]
**Police and protesters clash in [[Ivory Coast]], after the latter dismantled a half-built [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] testing center over fears that people using the facility would spread the virus through their district. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-ivorycoast-violenc/ivory-coast-police-clash-with-protesters-over-coronavirus-test-centre-idUSKBN21O1LT (Reuters)]
*[[Right-wing terrorism#Russia|Right-wing terrorism in Russia]], [[Russia–United States relations]]
**In an unprecedented move, the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] designates a [[white supremacist]] group, based in Russia, as a [[terrorism in Russia|terrorist]] organization, and imposes individual sanctions on its leaders. The organization, {{ill|Russian Imperial Movement|sv|Ryska imperiska rörelsen}}, is believed to have trained the perpetrators of a series of terrorist attacks in [[Gothenburg]], [[Sweden]], in 2016. [https://apnews.com/4f5dfda48d9f13876af828757c85d852 (Associated Press)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[2020 Wisconsin Democratic primary]], [[2020 Wisconsin Republican primary]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
***The [[Wisconsin Supreme Court]] overturns Governor [[Tony Evers]]'s order to postpone tomorrow's primary elections. Furthermore, the [[Supreme Court of the United States]] rules 5–4 in favor of the [[Republican National Committee]] to overturn a lower court decision extending [[absentee ballot]] eligibility in the [[Wisconsin]] primary election to those ballots postmarked by April 13, ruling that ballots postmarked after April 7 will be invalidated. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/04/06/wisconsin-governor-orders-stop-to-in-person-voting-on-eve-of-election-168527 (''Politico'')] [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/06/wisconsin-supreme-court-halts-absentee-ballot-deadline-extension.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]], [[2020 Polish presidential election]]
***Deputy Prime Minister [[Jarosław Gowin]] tenders resignation over disagreement with the ruling [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] (PiS) party as to the upcoming presidential election. He stated at a [[press conference]] that the election scheduled for May 10, should be postponed, while the government pushes for the election amid the coronavirus pandemic. Gowin also resigns as [[Ministry of Science and Higher Education (Poland)|Minister of Science and Higher Education]]. [https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7784/Artykul/2487977,UPDATE-Polish-deputy-PM-quits-amid-spat-over-election (Radio Poland)]
***[[Government of Poland|Polish]] MPs, with 230–226 votes and two abstained, pass a bill under which the presidential election in May will be held by postal vote only. The bill now goes to the upper house, the [[Senate of Poland|Senate]], for debate. [https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7784/Artykul/2488251,Polish-MPs-back-rules-to-hold-presidential-election-by-postal-vote-only (Radio Poland)]
